definition: Antagonistic means showing active opposition or hostility toward someone or something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word antagonistic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know antagonistic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The new moderator turned the once-friendly gardening forum antagonistic within a month, pinning quarrels at the top of every thread and deleting the apologies.
An unfriendly clerk just withholds the warmth; antagonistic is stronger — the opposition turns active, aimed at someone and working against them.
Belligerent goes further than antagonistic: an antagonistic opponent works against you, while a belligerent one is openly spoiling for the fight itself.

Hostile says the ill will is out in the open — a glare, a slammed door, a cold refusal all qualify, whether or not anything gets done about it. Antagonistic adds direction and effort: the ill will is organized into working against someone. A hostile silence radiates; an antagonistic campaign pushes back.

Confrontational names the appetite for the face-to-face clash itself: raising the issue directly, wanting the showdown. Antagonistic is wider — it covers any stance set against another side, including quiet obstruction that never raises its voice.
